title: Representation-based semantic addressing: can an injected representation reduce routing input without hidden-truth access?
question: Across held-out relations and candidate populations, does representation-based addressing preserve capability while reducing the number of candidates presented to the router?
hypothesis: A representation address index using an encoder trained only from public query/candidate information can retain acceptable candidates at bounded query-time bucket-probe cost, reducing router input relative to exhaustive routing. Exact content addressing remains the control.

arms.name: semantic_address
arms.intervention: use RepresentationAddressIndex with frozen encoder and bounded LSH probes

primary_endpoint.name: success_rate
primary_endpoint.definition: Observed task success using the environment evaluator after routing and execution.

required_controls: exact ContentAddressIndex remains a non-learned control
exhaustive routing remains the capability ceiling
encoder receives only public Query and PersistentState
hidden acceptable_actions and reference_bits are inaccessible to address encoders
no fallback from semantic address miss to exhaustive routing
training data is disjoint from evaluation seeds and held-out relation/population conditions

endpoints.name: success_rate
endpoints.description: Observed task success after the selected candidate is executed and verified.

endpoints.name: address_recall_at_k
endpoints.role: secondary — acceptable candidates retained by the address stage
endpoints.description: Fraction of environment-acceptable actions represented in the retained set.

endpoints.name: candidate_work_amortized
endpoints.role: secondary — build plus address plus router candidate work amortized over queries

decision_rule.condition: semantic_address success_rate remains within the exhaustive arm's seed spread while router_candidates_per_step is bounded by K and no hidden-truth access occurs
decision_rule.licenses: the representation-addressing boundary preserves capability under the registered synthetic conditions.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the encoder is learned, that it beats exact retrieval, or C5.

decision_rule.condition: semantic_address success_rate is materially below exhaustive while address_recall_at_k is also reduced
decision_rule.licenses: the current representation/addressing control loses relevant candidates under the registered budget.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that selective computation is impossible or that another encoder cannot recover the loss.

decision_rule.condition: router_candidates_per_step grows with H in the semantic arm
decision_rule.licenses: the runtime does not provide a bounded routing boundary.

held_constant: same candidate universes and evaluation seeds across arms
hidden acceptable actions and reference_bits never enter the address encoder
semantic misses fail closed; no exhaustive fallback
exact ContentAddressIndex remains the non-learned control
